engineering_plan.approach: Keep the existing synchronous engine and durable workflow contracts. Split three independent repairs into one parallel cohort: normalize worktree options inside the shared route branch; opt baseline operations into bounded short-lock waits and join active capture outside the cohort mutex; pre-scaffold planning invocations and finalize declared parent references through one common pre-validation materialization hook. Add no runtime dependencies or global queue.

components.name: Route selection
components.design: In routeDelivery, select one versus multiple chunks before applying worktreeName. Pass it only to startSingleDeliveryRun; cohort fan-out derives its own worktrees. Cover automatic operator/away approval and retry through the shared path. Keep existing dirty-tree, opt-out, idempotency, and failed-handoff behavior.

components.name: Shared baseline join
components.design: Add optional OperationMutexOptions to withCohortSession, defaulting to current immediate refusal. Baseline claim/record/release opt into a 5000 ms short-lock wait. Extend claimCohortBaselineCapture with optional join budget/progress options; the engine passes 3600000 ms while the primitive default stays fail-fast. Inspect state under the short lock, poll a live peer outside it at 100 ms using the existing synchronous wait pattern and a monotonic deadline, report joining immediately and each 60 seconds, adopt complete publication, and elect one replacement after a released or dead owner.

components.name: Baseline failure and provenance
components.design: Validate the claimant before record, retain foreign-release no-op behavior, preserve all baseline pointer/provenance and valid failed-diagnostic records, release on a thrown capture or environment-probe block, and never publish partial profile sets. Timeout diagnostics name the cohort, holder, elapsed budget, and ./bin/pan prepare <waiting-run-id>. Do not change unrelated run mutex policy.

components.name: Planning preparation
components.design: After the complete invocation/manifest is built, writeInvocationArtifacts invokes the existing scaffoldStageOutput for planning and creates operator/specs. Preserve authored output and untouched-scaffold semantics. Resolve the planning scaffold requirement to harness ownership without changing assessment, spotfix, or source-worker requirements.

components.name: Canonical reference finalization
components.design: Add finalizePlanningReferences in one small cohort specification module. Invoke it through materializeOutputSubmission after full-output or merge-patch resolution, before strict validators in both validation and submission. A documented harness-pending token is valid only in a draft. Build one canonical parent snapshot with buildContextReference, preflight every declared run-local path/block, atomically update only digest and owned reference-status metadata, audit changed paths, and reject concurrent parent changes. Restrict this to the active unratified planning invocation; never rewrite worker claims or ratified/foreign context. Pure validators remain strict and nonmutating.

Preserve executor restrictions, regenerate affected projections/function indexes through existing automation, and leave release and intake reconciliation with the integrated release owner.

The scaffold and reference builder already supply the necessary deterministic primitives, but preparation does not yet wire them for planning and finalization is proposed work. # TRACE friction repair: parent specification

## Status

Planning draft for run `63264_Oct-15-1082_trace-fricti`, invocation
`01_plan-1_7a2e6888`. This is not a ratified plan. The substantive plan is
recorded below; canonical child-reference finalization is blocked by the
current execution capability. No source changes, workflow lifecycle actions,
or validation commands were performed by this planner.

## Request and evidence

The operator requests repairs for TRACE-08, TRACE-09, and TRACE-04, using
managed worktree `trace-friction-parallel`. Source paths below resolve in
`/Users/alen/Dev/pancreator/worktrees/operator/trace-friction-parallel`.
Runtime paths and commands resolve in `/Users/alen/Dev/pancreator`.

The original request is
`runtime/logs/workflows/63264_Oct-15-1082_trace-fricti/operator/request.md`.
The complete intake was read by reference:

- Source: `runtime/inbox/queue/63265_Oct-14-0900_trace-copilo-run-friction.md`
- Selected range: the complete file.
- Content digest: `sha256:873219a680b28a42d4c71deaa396b8685b3a295a497164db6367e62a54205541`
- Read when: consult the intake before a decision about the originating findings or scope outside a chunk.

The authorized definitions are TRACE-04 at lines 162-172, TRACE-08 at
199-206, and TRACE-09 at 207-214. The intake's repair constraints are at
430-438. Other findings supply context, not additional authorization.

## Product specification

### Summary

An approved plan bound to a managed worktree must route successfully whether
it contains one chunk or several. Sibling delivery runs must be able to
prepare concurrently while sharing one pre-implementation baseline. A
planner without shell access must be able to produce complete planning
artifacts through harness-provided scaffolding and canonical reference
finalization.

### User stories

- US-01: As an operator approving a worktree-bound plan, I want the harness to select the correct delivery route without an incompatible worktree argument stopping fan-out. Origin: TRACE-08.
- US-02: As a supervisor preparing ready siblings together, I want them to join one shared baseline capture, so ordinary concurrency does not require sequential recovery. Origin: TRACE-09.
- US-03: As a planner with file tools but no shell, I want output preparation and parent-reference bookkeeping to be executable within my contract, including revisions of the parent. Origin: TRACE-04.

### Constraints

- C-01: Preserve the existing run and operator-owned approval. This stage produces planning artifacts only; source repairs begin in later authorized delivery runs.
- C-02: Use the selected managed worktree as the planning/integration context. Each parallel delivery chunk receives its own branch and worktree; release preparation happens once after integration through the existing release authority.
- C-03: Keep exactly one shared baseline per required interior profile, including its capture workspace, capturer, artifact, fingerprint, configuration checks, and existing diagnostic-delta semantics. Never capture the release/full profile merely to prepare a sibling.
- C-04: Keep the planner's restricted tool policy. Do not grant an unrestricted shell or directory capability merely for output bookkeeping.
- C-05: Use the canonical trimmed-content reference basis. Never invent, zero-fill, or hand-calculate a digest; every declared child must reach the final parent by an audited reference. A parent revision refreshes all dependent references before ratification.
- C-06: Preserve single-chunk explicit/default worktree selection, approval durability, routing opt-out, failed-route recovery, and idempotent reuse of existing runs or sessions.
- C-07: Keep target/source ownership and secret protections. Do not inspect or patch third-party compiled code, dependency trees, or caches. Preserve partial-evidence versus completed-verdict distinctions.
- C-08: Supply repair evidence for the three authorized findings and a handoff to the integrated release owner to extend the intake and reconcile them against repair and release commits after delivery and release.

### Out of scope

- OOS-01: Repairs to TRACE-01 through TRACE-28 other than TRACE-04, TRACE-08, and TRACE-09, even where the intake reports related symptoms.
- OOS-02: Native UI fixes, telemetry streaming, usage aggregation, invented cost estimates, and summing duplicate modelMetrics/agentMetrics views. This plan makes no claim that those surfaces are repaired.
- OOS-03: Changing active configuration, model/executor mappings, verification level, operator approvals, publication authority, or release metadata during this planning stage.

### Questions and dispositions

- Q-01: What does a worktree selection mean for each route?
  Resolved: `src/cli/args.ts::deliveryRouteOptions` forwards `--worktree`;
  `src/lib/cohorts/delivery.ts::routeDelivery` rejects that option for
  multiple chunks, while the single route uses it. Select the route first,
  pass the option to the single route only, and let a cohort continue to
  derive distinct worktrees. Evidence: those current source functions,
  `DeliveryRouteOptions` in `src/lib/cohorts/state.ts`, and TRACE-08.
- Q-02: Why are sibling preparations incompatible with current baseline coordination?
  Resolved: `prepareInvocation` holds a per-run lock, but
  `withCohortSession` refuses a live session lock immediately.
  `claimCohortBaselineCapture` also throws on a different live capturer;
  capture itself runs outside the session lock. Both the brief mutex race
  and the long-lived claim need coordination. Evidence:
  `src/lib/engine/prepare.ts`, `src/lib/cohorts/state.ts`,
  `src/lib/cohorts/baselines.ts`, `src/lib/engine/baselines.ts`, and
  `src/lib/io.ts::withOperationMutex`. This explains current code; it does
  not assert which lock a historical process held.
- Q-03: How can no-shell planning satisfy scaffolding and canonical digest requirements?
  Resolved as an architecture decision: make these bounded operations
  harness-owned. Preparation invokes the existing scaffold helper and
  creates the specification directory. A common pre-validation finalizer
  uses `buildContextReference` to write only declared child-reference
  metadata. Evidence: current `writeInvocationArtifacts` omits output
  scaffolding, `scaffoldStageOutput` already supplies the required shape,
  `buildContextReference` documents the same trimmed basis as the digest
  command, and both submission paths materialize an output through
  `materializeOutputSubmission`. TRACE-04 and the current tool inventory
  establish the capability gap. This finalizer is proposed work, not an
  existing feature.

No question asks what an earlier commit removed or guaranteed. No historical
change is inferred from the present workspace.

## Engineering plan

### Architecture

Use the existing synchronous engine, durable cohort records, scaffold
automation, reference helper, and strict validators. Add no dependency,
framework, scheduler, broad retry layer, or alternate workflow.

#### Routing

Normalize worktree selection at the route branch in
`src/lib/cohorts/delivery.ts`, shared by automatic approval and explicit
retry. A cohort route accepts the command's workspace targeting context
without forwarding a single delivery worktree into fan-out. The route
continues to derive each chunk worktree, check a committed planning tree,
reuse an existing session, and record a concrete failure and retry command
for actual failures. Keep single-delivery routing unchanged. Cover the CLI
approval boundary, not only a helper call.

#### Baseline coordination

Keep the per-run prepare lock and the short cohort state critical section.
Extend `withCohortSession` with optional `OperationMutexOptions`; its default
remains immediate refusal. Only baseline claim/record/release operations opt
into a bounded 5,000 ms wait for the short session update.

Extend `claimCohortBaselineCapture` with optional bounded join/progress
options. The default preserves its low-level immediate-refusal behavior.
`ensureWorkflowRepositoryCheckBaselines` opts into joining for up to
3,600,000 ms. Inspect the durable baseline/claim under the short lock; when
another live process owns capture, release the lock and poll at 100 ms
outside it. Use the repository's synchronous `Atomics.wait` pattern rather
than shell timers. Emit a join message immediately and a progress update at
least every 60 seconds. Use a monotonic elapsed-time budget.

After publication, adopt the recorded pointers. After claim release or a
dead owner, reacquire under the lock and elect exactly one replacement.
Record validates the current claimant before publishing; foreign release
keeps its existing no-op semantics. Baseline collection and repository
checks stay outside the session lock. Preserve valid failed-check baseline
records; an environment-probe failure or thrown capture does not publish a
partial collection and releases its claim.

Timeouts identify cohort, holder, elapsed bound, and the exact
`./bin/pan prepare <waiting-run-id>` recovery command. A timeout is an
explicit incomplete preparation, never an empty or passing baseline.
Ordinary unrelated run operations keep their existing fail-fast behavior.
The one-hour join and five-second update bounds are engineering defaults,
not new operator policy or test-runtime targets. Tests inject short budgets
and use deterministic process barriers instead of long real waits.

#### No-shell planning

After an invocation's manifest and output contract are complete,
`writeInvocationArtifacts` invokes `scaffoldStageOutput` for planning
invocations and ensures the run's `operator/specs/` directory exists.
Preserve idempotence and refuse to overwrite worker-authored output.
An untouched scaffold must still be recognized by watch as unfinished.

Add one small module, `src/lib/cohorts/specifications.ts`, exporting
`finalizePlanningReferences`. Its input is the active planning invocation
and materialized output; it operates only on the parent and children
declared in that output under the current run's specification directory.
A worker may write `harness-pending` in the draft reference digest field.
That is a declared draft token, never an accepted digest.

Invoke the helper from the common `materializeOutputSubmission` path used
by output validation and submission, after full-output or merge-patch
materialization, before strict plan/child validators. Both paths therefore
see the same final references. Document that draft artifact finalization
can occur while validation leaves workflow state unchanged. Direct
validator entry points stay pure and still reject a pending or stale
reference.

Preflight every declared path and reference block before any writes.
Reject paths outside the active run, traversal, symlink escapes, a parent
used as a child, duplicate children, missing files, or ambiguous blocks.
Use the existing `buildContextReference`, including its canonical trimming,
and existing atomic writes. Update only digest and explicitly
harness-owned reference-status metadata. Do not rewrite scope, acceptance
criteria, proof tags, worker results, risks, or self-evaluations.

Finalize every declared child against one parent snapshot, verify that the
parent has not changed before accepting the result, and report a concurrent
edit as an explicit failure requiring a fresh finalization. A failed write
